problems.title: Perpendicular planes
problems.question: For which a are ax−6y+3z−1=0 and 3x−2y+z+2a−1=0 perpendicular?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: Their normals are $(a,-6,3)$ and $(3,-2,1)$; perpendicular planes have perpendicular normals.

problems.title: Minimum of a positive-variable function
problems.question: Find the minimum of $16/x+x^2+1$, x>0.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: The function decreases until x=2 and increases thereafter. Its value there is 8+4+1.

problems.title: Hyperbola parameters
problems.question: A hyperbola has asymptotes y=±.75x and focus separation 30. Choose its equation.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: Set a=4k, b=3k, giving 25k²=225 and k=3. Thus a=12, b=9.

problems.title: Recover a function from its derivative
problems.question: f′(x)=$8x/\sqrt{2x^2+1}$ and f(0)=5. Find f(2).
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.

problems.title: Inflection of a logarithmic quotient
problems.question: Find the inflection-point x-coordinate of $f(x)=\ln(6x)/(2x)$.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: For x>0 the denominator is positive. The numerator changes sign where ln(6x)=3/2.

problems.title: Reflect a point in a plane
problems.question: Reflect A=(1,2,1) in x+y+z=0. Find the product of the reflected coordinates.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: A·n=4, n·n=3, so B=(−5/3,−2/3,−5/3). Multiply its coordinates.

problems.title: Join two equal-slope tangent points
problems.question: On $y=x^3/3-2x^2-4x+31/3$, tangents at A, B are parallel to y=x+199. Find line AB.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: The derivative is $x^2-4x-4$. Set it to slope 1.
steps: x²−4x−5=0 gives x=−1,5. Their function values are 12,−18. The joining slope is (−18−12)/6=−5, giving intercept 7.

problems.title: Integrate a second derivative
problems.question: f″(x)=36x−10, f(0)=−3, f(1)=0. Find f(−1).
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: D=−3, and f(1)=0 gives C=2. Substitute x=−1: −6−5−2−3.

problems.title: Positive tangent intercepts
problems.question: For $f(x)=460-x^3/300-8100/x$, x>0, find x where the tangent meets both positive coordinate axes.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: The slope is $m=-x^2/100+8100/x^2$. Its y-intercept is $b=f-xf\prime=460+x^3/150-16200/x$.
steps: Both intercepts are positive exactly when b>0 and m<0. The slope is negative for x>30. At 30, b=100, and b′=x²/50+16200/x²>0, so b stays positive for all x>30.

problems.title: Definite integral of a sine power
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/2}3\sin^2x\cos x\, dx$.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: Evaluate at the bounds: 1³−(1/2)³.

problems.title: Which points lie in a plane?
problems.question: A=(1,2,−1), B=(3,−2,1), C=(1,0,1). Which of D=(2,2,2), E=(−1,4,−1), K=(0,0,3) lie in ABC?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: The plane is $x+y+z=2$, since all three noncollinear defining points satisfy it.
steps: D’s coordinate sum is 6, E’s is 2, K’s is 3.

problems.title: Angle between two planes
problems.question: Find the angle between x+2y−2z−3=0 and 2x−y+2z+3=0.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: Normals (1,2,−2),(2,−1,2) have dot product −4 and both length 3. Thus cosθ=4/9.
problems.note: None of 15°,30°,45°,60°,90° equals this; the printed “none of the preceding answers” choice is correct.

problems.title: Parabola directrix and a line
problems.question: Find the coordinate sum of the intersection of the directrix of y²=−12x and y=5x+1.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: Substitute x=3 into the line to get y=16.

problems.title: A common conic definition
problems.question: Which property is common to ellipse, hyperbola and parabola?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: A conic can be defined by $PF=e\,\operatorname{dist}(P,\ell)$ for a focus F and directrix ℓ.
steps: For an ellipse 0<e<1; for a parabola e=1; for a hyperbola e>1. Thus the focus–directrix description applies to all three noncircular conics.
problems.note: A circle is the limiting ellipse with e=0; it has no finite directrix. The usual school focus–directrix statement for ellipses concerns the noncircular case.

problems.title: An oblique asymptote
problems.question: Find the listed asymptote of $y=x-2/x+1/x^3$.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: The graph approaches y=x at either end.

problems.title: A decreasing interval
problems.question: Which listed interval is a decreasing interval for $y=x-2/x+1/x^3$?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: For x≠0 the denominator and x²+3 are positive. Thus y′<0 when 0<|x|<1. Among the choices, (0,1] is valid.

problems.title: Area between sideways parabolas
problems.question: Find the are a between y²=4−x and y²=12+3x.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: The width is 8−4y²/3. Integrate from −√6 to √6: [8y−4y³/9] at those limits.

problems.title: What a second derivative forces
problems.question: $f\prime\prime(x)=3(x+1)^3(x-2)(x-4)^2$. I: inflection at 2; II: inflection at 4; III: local maximum at −1. Which must hold?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: An odd-multiplicity zero of f″ changes concavity; an even-multiplicity zero does not.
steps: At 2 concavity changes, so I is true. At 4 the squared factor does not change sign, so II is false. A local maximum requires information about f′; adding any linear term changes f′ without changing f″, so III is not forced.

problems.title: A natural-valued area
problems.question: Area S lies below y=6x² above the x-axis for −a≤x≤a, with natural a. Which listed S can occur?
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: Among the printed numbers 1 through 6, only 4 has this for m, at a=1.

problems.title: Fundamental theorem of calculus
problems.question: $f(w)=\int_1^w\sqrt{x^3+2}\, dx$. Find f′(2).
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: At w=2 the value is √(8+2).

problems.title: Ellipse focus coordinates
problems.question: F=(m, c) is a focus of $x^2/9+y^2/16=1$. Find 10+m²−c².
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: The major axis is vertical, so $m=0$, $c^2=16-9=7$.
steps: Substitute 10+0−7.

problems.title: Integrate a product with its derivative
problems.question: f(2)=2 and $g(x)=(xf(x))\prime$. Find $\int_0^2xf(x)g(x)\, dx$.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: Let $u=xf(x)$. Then the integrand is $uu\prime$ and its antiderivative is $u^2/2$.
steps: At 2, u=4. At 0, u=0 because f is defined there. The integral is (16−0)/2.

problems.title: A hyperbola chord through the centre
problems.question: Opposite points A, B on $x^2/32-y^2/18=1$ have tangents parallel to 9x−4y+11=0. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
formulas: Implicit differentiation gives $y\prime=9x/(16y)$. Set it equal to $9/4$, hence $x=4y$.
steps: Substitution gives (4/9)y²=1, so y=±3/2 and x=±6. The distance between the opposite points is √(12²+3²).

problems.title: Maximise x plus y squared
problems.question: On $x^2/16+y^2/2=1$, maximise $x+y^2$.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: The maximum occurs at x=4, y=0, which is on the ellipse.

problems.title: A truncated exponential domain
problems.question: f(x)=$e^{2x}-6e^x+5$ on all real x, and g has the same formula for x≤a. Find the least a for which their minima agree.
problems.idea: Use derivatives, coordinates, or the standard geometric definition.
steps: The unique minimum −4 occurs at eˣ=3, or x=ln3. The restricted domain includes it precisely when a≥ln3.
